title: Diameter of Binary Tree
keyIdea: Every path has one highest node where it bends; there its length is left height + right height (in edges). So compute heights bottom-up like Max Depth, and at every node update diameter = max(diameter, lh + rh).

approaches.name: Brute force: heights at every node
approaches.idea: At each node, compute both subtree heights from scratch and check lh + rh; recurse into both children.
approaches.why: height() is O(size of subtree) and it's called again at every node: O(n²) on a chain.

approaches.name: One pass: height + diameter by reference
approaches.idea: height() returns 1 + max(lh, rh) as usual, and on the way updates diameter with lh + rh.
approaches.why: Each height is computed once and reused by its parent.

quiz.q: Why is the path through a node lh + rh (not lh + rh + 1)?
options: Diameter counts edges; heights count nodes below, which equals the edges on each side from this node

quiz.q: Does the diameter have to pass through the root?
options: No: it bends at whichever node gives the biggest lh + rh
Only if the root has two children

quiz.q: Why is diameter passed by reference?
options: The function already returns the height, so the diameter is updated on the side
